data.title: Allstate Joins Growing List of Companies Hit by Tech Outages — WSJ
data.description:
By Jean Eaglesham

A multiday tech outage at Allstate has left the insurer's customers struggling to renew policies, make claims or summon roadside help in Thanksgiving week.

Allstate's website and app have been down since Monday, according to online reports from its agents and customers. The outage impacts both homeowners and drivers, and coincides with Thanksgiving travel and a powerful nor'easter that slammed the East Coast.

The disruption is the latest in a string of recent technology outages that have affected a swath of everyday life, including email access, banking services and air travel. Many entities affected by these outages — such as Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, Chase, Apple and United Airlines — have said that the root problem wasn't a hack. In most cases, it was a system upgrade gone wrong.

Allstate hasn't said what is causing the outage or how long it is likely to last.

The company in a statement Wednesday said customers affected by the "service interruptions" won't lose coverage or be charged late fees as a result. "Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices," the statement added. A spokesman for Allstate declined to comment further Friday.

Early Friday, a message on Allstate's roadside-assistance online link said: "Our site is currently down for maintenance. Please check back later." Customers trying to log in to its website were told the company is working to restore access to services "as soon as possible." The site advised anyone wanting to file or manage a claim to call a customer-service line.

A spate of angry social-media posts from Allstate customers included people saying they were unable to order a tow, register a new car, close a mortgage or pay premiums. Some Allstate agents complained online of being unable to help customers or sell policies; some of these posts were later taken down.

The company insures 26 million drivers and eight million homeowners, according to its securities filings.

Lawmakers in Oklahoma, where Allstate is being sued by the state attorney general over its claims handling, called on the company Wednesday to "clearly communicate" with its customers about their options during the outage. Policyholders "should not be penalized for something completely outside their control," the heads of Oklahoma House Insurance Committee said in a statement. Allstate has denied the allegations in the lawsuit, which alleges it unfairly denied or underpaid claims for wind and hail damage.

The tech problem comes as Allstate is investing heavily in computing power. The insurer plans to launch AI-powered sales early next year. Its "personal agentic assistant" will be able to interact with customers' agents, Allstate Chief Executive Tom Wilson told investors this month.

"We're now marketing to machines and people," he said.

Write to Jean Eaglesham at Jean.Eaglesham@wsj.com

data.title: Mahindra Manulife opens hybrid long-short fund offer
data.description:
Mahindra Manulife Mutual Fund has launched the MSIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, an interval investment strategy that invests in equity and debt securities, with limited short exposure through derivatives. It is offered under the fund house’s Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) platform, MSIF.

The New Fund Offer opens on 27 November 2026 and closes on 11 December 2026. Continuous sale and repurchase will begin on 21 December 2026.

Equity Investments

The strategy plans to invest 65-75 per cent in equity and equity-related instruments, including arbitrage positions, and 25-35 per cent in debt and money market instruments. Up to 10 per cent may go into InvITs. The fund may take unhedged short positions of up to 25 per cent of net assets, use option strategies within regulatory limits, and participate in special situations such as IPOs, buybacks, mergers and demergers.

Anthony Heredia, MD and CEO of Mahindra Manulife Investment Management, said the fund combines fixed income and arbitrage with long and short equity positions. Krishna Sanghavi, Chief Investment Officer (Equity), said short positions will follow the same research discipline as long positions.

The fund will be managed by Aalap Shah and Abhishek Jaiswal for equity, and Amit Garg and Kush Sonigara for fixed income. It will be benchmarked against the CRISIL Hybrid 50+50 – Moderate Index and carries an AMFI Risk Band Level 2 at the NFO stage, which may change once investments are made.

The company noted that investments in Specialized Investment Funds carry relatively higher risk, including potential loss of capital and liquidity risk.

data.title: US stock market today: Dow, Nasdaq futures climb as tech stocks recover
data.description:
US stock futures rose sharply on Friday, November 27, as Wall Street prepared to resume trading after the Thanksgiving holiday, with technology and semiconductor stocks rebounding following a volatile week.

Futures tied to the S&P 500 climbed nearly 2%, while Nasdaq-100 futures advanced around 2.8%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gained 655 points, or about 1.3%, indicating a positive start to the shortened trading session.

The gains came as investors reassessed concerns over the profitability of artificial intelligence investments, allowing technology stocks to recover some of their recent losses.

Semiconductor stocks led the premarket rebound. Nvidia shares rose nearly 4%, while Micron gained around 6% in premarket trading.

The broader market has remained volatile through November, with investors weighing concerns over elevated technology stock valuations and the returns from heavy investments in artificial intelligence.

Meanwhile, crude oil prices moved higher, with Brent crude rising to around $92 per barrel, following increased attacks by Houthi militants on energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

US Treasury yields continued to decline despite stronger-than-expected economic growth data. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.84%, even after US GDP expanded at an annualised rate of 4.3% in the third quarter.

Global markets trade higher

Asian and European markets also traded largely higher on Friday.

Japan's Nikkei 225 advanced 0.3%, while South Korea's Kospi gained 0.6%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.4%.

In Europe, Germany's DAX climbed around 1%, while the UK's FTSE 100 gained 0.65%. France's CAC 40 was up 0.35%.

Wall Street heads into final session after volatile week

The positive start follows a turbulent week for US equities. Markets began the week on a strong note, with Nvidia shares surging 31% on Monday, helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite post their strongest single-day gains since April 2025.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average also rallied more than 1,400 points, or approximately 3%, during the session.

However, the rally subsequently lost momentum, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq coming under pressure as Nvidia and other artificial intelligence-linked stocks gave back some of their earlier gains.

US markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and are scheduled to operate for a shortened session on Friday. The stock market will close at 1 pm ET, while bond trading will end at 2 pm ET.

data.title: Columbia Financial, Inc. Announces CFO Transition
data.description:
Resignation of CFO Thomas Splaine, Jr.; Appointment of Dennis E. Gibney as Interim CFOCompany to Commence Search for Permanent Chief Financial Officer

FAIR LAWN, N.J., Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Columbia Financial, Inc. (the “Company”) , the holding company for Columbia Bank (“Bank”), today announced that Thomas Splaine, Jr., Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of the Company and the Bank, has notified the Company and the Bank of his intent to resign from the Company and the Bank effective December 18, 2026 for personal reasons. Mr. Splaine’s resignation of employment did not result from any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company’s financial statements, operations, policies, or practices.

In connection with Mr. Splaine’s departure, Dennis E. Gibney, First Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Banking Officer of the Company and the Bank, has been appointed Interim Chief Financial Officer effective December 18, 2026. Mr. Gibney previously served as Chief Financial Officer of the Company and the Bank from 2014 through January 28, 2026. He will continue in his other positions at the Company and the Bank while he serves as Interim Chief Financial Officer.

The Company has engaged an executive search firm and commenced a search for a permanent Chief Financial Officer.

About Columbia Financial, Inc.

Columbia Financial, Inc. is a Maryland corporation organized as Columbia Bank's parent holding company. Columbia Bank is a federally chartered savings bank headquartered in Fair Lawn, New Jersey that operates more than 100 full-service banking offices and offers traditional financial services to consumers and businesses in its market area, including select counties in New Jersey, and Brooklyn and Staten Island New York.

data.title: US futures rally on AI rebound after bruising month, Treasuries dip
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq futures rally 2.1% as AI trade rebounds
  • European stocks rise while US Treasuries slip
  • Chinese stocks jump more than 4% on new support measures

By Harry Robertson and Stella Qiu

US futures rose sharply on Friday while Asian and European stocks rallied, with a holiday lull giving some respite from the AI jitters that have weighed heavily on markets this month.

Nasdaq futures rallied 2.1% and S&P 500 futures were 1.5% higher after Wall Street was shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

European stocks rose 0.8%, building on a 1.7% gain the previous day.

Japan's Nikkei jumped 2.1% overnight, while MSCI's index of Asian shares excluding Japan (.MISX00000PUS) climbed 1.8%.

"It is quite possible that the rebound could go further," Shane Oliver, chief economist at AMP, said.

He cited factors such as the return of Jensen Huang to chipmaking giant Nvidia , the resilient US economy, strong corporate profit growth and December being a seasonally stronger period for shares.

"However, the risk of a deeper correction at some point in the next six months remains high."

Meanwhile, China's blue chips gained 4.2%, a day after hitting their lowest since June 2025, as the cabinet rolled out more support for capital markets, calling for a greater role by state-backed "national team" investors.

Global equities have slid in erratic trading in recent weeks as doubts have crept in about whether huge rallies in AI stocks will be justified by future earnings.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 traded roughly 20% lower than its October record high on Wednesday, before rebounding later in the session. MSCI's all-world stock index is down 5% for the month EURONEXT:IACWI.

Huang's dramatic departure from and return to Nvidia has been a major source of volatility.

Shares in the $3.6-trillion company surged 31% when Huang was reinstated on Monday but remain down 27% for the month.

Nvidia remained a source of unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade.

TREASURIES GIVE UP GAINS

US Treasuries have gained as the stock selloff has pushed investors towards safe-haven assets, but were on the back foot on Friday as equities rallied.

The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield rose 5 basis points to 4.90%, putting it roughly flat for the week after a sharp drop a week earlier. Yields move inversely to prices.

The US dollar was flat on the day but headed for a third monthly gain that has pushed it to its highest since March 2025.

Expectations that the Federal Reserve is almost certain to lift interest rates in December have boosted the currency, as have safe-haven flows.

The euro was little changed after news that Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos would become the next president of the European Central Bank, a well-telegraphed move that suggested policy continuity. European yields ticked higher.

Futures imply a 99% chance the Fed will raise rates in December, but speculation of a half-point increase has faded. (0#USDIRPR)

Bond investors are wondering if losses in global stocks and doubts about AI-driven investment might make central banks less hawkish.

"The Fed could, of course, still blink," David Rees, chief economist at Schroders, said. "But a Fed put would not necessarily be unambiguously positive for markets."

"If growth and inflation data remain firm, in a game of cat and mouse, markets could soon begin pricing a more hawkish Fed back in, potentially setting off the same chain of events all over again."

Oil prices were heading for the first weekly rise in four on renewed concerns about supply disruptions. Brent crude futures rose to a more than two-week high of $98 a barrel on Friday, although they were down around 17% for the month.

data.title: Oil Prices Mixed Ahead of OPEC+ Meeting as Middle East Supply Risks Persist — Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid

DOHA, Qatar--Oil prices were mixed on Friday as traders weighed renewed threats to Middle Eastern supplies ahead of a meeting of OPEC and its allies during the weekend.

Brent crude futures were broadly flat at $96.56 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate rose 1.8% to $85.15 a barrel. Both benchmarks pared earlier gains, having traded at $97.15 and $85.96 a barrel, respectively.

The two indicators are on track for their first weekly gain this month as geopolitical risks in the Middle East intensify, analysts at MUFG said in a note Friday.

The premium on front-month Brent futures over the following month's contract has widened to $4.28 a barrel from around $2.50 at the start of the week, the analysts said. The impact of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting on oil prices is likely to be tempered by the outlook for the regional conflict, they added.

Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said Thursday that an attack on the Jazan oil refinery sparked a fire and temporarily halted some operations. Authorities were assessing the damage and checking the safety of the facilities, the ministry said.

Meanwhile, an Iranian drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians, The Wall Street Journal reported. Iran denied responsibility for the attack, which comes as negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain deadlocked despite a ceasefire.

Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain at just 31% of prewar levels, according to preliminary data from Kpler. While Iraqi crude exports remain relatively strong, delays to some November and December cargoes have raised concerns over the reliability of near-term Middle Eastern supplies, Alex Booth, head of research at the data provider, said.

The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and other producers in the broader group called OPEC+ are expected to discuss their collective output policy for 2027 on Sunday, with existing production agreements set to expire at the end of this year.

The group's assessment of members' sustainable production capacities will help determine individual output quotas for next year. However, disruptions to production and exports during the Iran war have complicated efforts to establish how much individual countries can pump.

It remains unclear whether Saudi Arabia--the cartel's de-facto leader--and other members will restore more supply, maintain current restrictions or consider fresh cuts to support prices.

Sunday's meeting could end without a final decision, leaving current production quotas in place for the time being, Commerzbank analyst Barbara Lambrecht said. With the exception of Iraq, most OPEC+ members are producing well below their existing quotas, while some countries, including Russia, are unable to increase output further, she said.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com

data.title: IOCL faces Karnataka notice after inspection finds excess ethanol delivery, short supply of petrol
data.description:
The Karnataka government has issued a show-cause notice to IOCL over discrepancies in the measurement of ethanol and motor gasoline at its Devanagonthi terminal near Bengaluru, with inspections by the Legal Metrology Department detecting a breach in permissible proportions.

Inspection detects excess ethanol, short delivery of petrol

The inspection, conducted on November 25 using a verified master proving measure, found excess delivery of 14 litres of ethanol for every 3,000 litres measured in one of the mass flow meters, while motor gasoline was short-delivered by four to six litres for the same quantity, according to the government notice.

Another ethanol mass flow meter was found to be delivering three litres in excess for every 3,000 litres measured, the notice said.

“After the Karnataka Government exposed over-blending of ethanol in petrol beyond the prescribed E20 limit, our Legal Metrology Department has begun inspecting Oil Marketing Company (OMC) terminals, where the blending is carried out,” Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad said in a Facebook post on Friday.

The minister said the inspection findings were beyond permissible limits and that a show-cause notice has been issued under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.

IOCL asked to explain discrepancies within seven days

In its notice to the Deputy General Manager and terminal in-charge of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)’s Devanagonthi facility, the department sought an explanation for the discrepancies, details of the latest calibration and maintenance of the measuring equipment, and corrective measures to ensure compliance with the law.

The company has been directed to submit its written explanation, along with verification certificates, calibration and maintenance records, within seven days of receiving the notice.

It has also been directed not to use the concerned measuring systems for further commercial transactions until their accuracy and compliance with statutory requirements are established. Failure to submit a satisfactory explanation could invite further legal and departmental action, the notice said.

Action follows Karnataka’s E20 petrol blending allegations

The latest action comes amid a row involving the Karnataka government and public sector oil marketing companies over alleged blending of ethanol in petrol beyond the prescribed 20 per cent limit.

On November 6, Arshad alleged that petrol supplied by major OMCs contained ethanol beyond the prescribed E20 limit. Tests on samples collected from seven districts recorded levels as high as 31.2 per cent in IOCL petrol and 30.5 per cent in HPCL petrol.

The same day, IOCL, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), in a joint statement, rejected the allegations, saying the findings were not based on testing conducted in accordance with prescribed statutory and technical procedures.

They maintained that the E20 petrol supplied by them conformed to the Bureau of Indian Standards specification IS 17021.

On November 9, Arshad reiterated that the state government stood by its findings and challenged the OMCs to explain the ethanol content in 63 samples collected from petrol pumps across Karnataka.

data.title: Dollar set for flat week, still close to 22-month peak
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar unchanged after Thanksgiving, set for modest weekly rise
  • Risk-sensitive currencies rise with US stock futures
  • Dollar garners support from higher US yields, safe-haven demand

By Stefano Rebaudo

The dollar was still close to its highest level in 22 months after a the tech rout drove investors towards safe-haven assets.

The dollar index started its rally in early November and hit a 22-month high of 104.53 earlier this week. It was last little changed at 103.80 and on track for a modest weekly rise of about 0.03%.

US stock futures rose on Friday as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday with renewed appetite for beaten-down shares, following a seesawing of AI stocks this week as investors weighed more attractive valuations against persistent concerns about heavy spending on the technology.

"We expect the Fed to remain hawkish and the US economy resilient, and our multi-asset strategists remain upbeat on US equities and the AI theme," said Daragh Maher, senior forex strategist at HSBC.

"The main risk to our view is that renewed market weakness could erode rate support, with no guarantee that safe-haven demand would again compensate," he said, adding that December’s Fed rate forecasts would be pivotal to the bullish cyclical greenback story.

If the tech rout fades, investors may strengthen expectations of Federal Reserve tightening, boosting Treasury yields and the dollar's yield appeal, even as improving risk sentiment curbs demand for the currency as a safe haven.

However investors remained cautious despite Friday's sharp rise in US stock futures.

"The high-beta Australian dollar, Kiwi dollar and Norwegian krone are leading gains in G10, although the moves remain modest compared with their recent losses," Francesco Pesole, forex strategist at ING, said.

"That suggests the forward-looking forex market remains cautious about calling an all-clear on risk sentiment," he added.

A so-called high-beta currency tends to amplify shifts in global sentiment, outperforming when risk appetite improves and underperforming when it fades.

The Norwegian crown rose 0.25% to 9.74 versus the greenback.

The Aussie dollar added 0.70% to $0.667, finding its feet after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday.

The New Zealand dollar was also supported by results of the general election, which reduced political uncertainty, even with no clear winner.

Geopolitics remained in the background but oil prices were on track to snap a three-week losing streak following attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure.

Higher Brent crude futures often underpin the dollar against the euro and yen, as they boost revenues for US energy exporters while increasing import costs for the euro zone and Japan.

The euro was roughly unchanged at $1.0964 with investors showing little reaction to news that Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos was set to be nominated as the head of the European Central Bank.

DOLLAR/YEN 160 LEVEL BACK IN FOCUS

The US currency was steady at 159.27 yen amid concerns about another round of Japanese intervention.

Data showed that annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike as soon as next month.

"The yen is understandably weaker today given the strong rebound in risk that has helped lift US Treasury bond yields," Derek Halpenny, strategist at MUFG, said.

"Better risk conditions could quickly bring back focus on intervention especially if we get a hawkish hike from the FOMC on December 9."

Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields rose 5 bps to 4.90%.
